text:
maya: Quick sync — trying to land the console UX for automatic fallback policies. Main questions: what should the default "soft degrade" behavior be, how do we expose error triggers, and what's the minimum audit sampling we need so Support can investigate without burning logs. TL;DR: need safe defaults + a compact expert mode.

alex: +1 on safe defaults. From runtime side we want: 1) explicit activation window (eg 30s sustained errors) 2) a revert TTL (eg 10m) 3) sample every Nth fallback event for full trace. Keep defaults conservative.

sam: For SRE: audit events must include request id, route, active policy id, chosen fallback model/route, and a short reason code. We can't store full request bodies by default, so sampling matters. Suggest: default sample 1% + on-demand 100% capture for a selected timeframe.

li: Product perspective: make the primary control a 3-state switch: Monitor-only -> Soft-degrade (route to fallback but mark telemetry) -> Hard-degrade (return lighter responses / block expensive ops). Expose threshold sliders under "Advanced". Default to Monitor-only for first 24h after policy creation, then auto-enforce if user opts in.

rachel: Draft of a compact policy JSON to show in the UI's "expert" view: 
```json
{
  "policy_id": "policy-1234",
  "mode": "soft_degrade",
  "trigger": {
    "metric": "error_rate",
    "window_secs": 30,
    "threshold_pct": 5
  },
  "revert_ttl_secs": 600,
  "audit_sampling": {
    "baseline_pct": 1,
    "on_trigger_pct": 100
  }
}
```
This keeps it compact but expressive. We should show a one-line summary in the editor: "Soft degrade on >5% errors over 30s, revert after 10m, sample 1% (full capture on trigger)".

alex: Two pragmatic notes: 1) When soft_degrade routes to a cheaper model, we need a billing flag so customers know unit cost changed. 2) Circuit oscillation: add a small hysteresis (eg require 2 consecutive windows) or an exponential backoff on re-enables to avoid flip-flop.

sam: Agree re hysteresis. Also we need an incident-friendly "capture now" button in the console that temporarily raises sampling to 100% and pins audit logs for N mins. That should be audit-logged itself (who clicked it).

maya: UI proposals: main policy card with mode chip, small inline KPI preview (error rate sparkline, current sample rate). Controls: threshold slider, window dropdown (15s/30s/60s), revert TTL input, and a secondary "simulate" button that runs a dry-run on recent telemetry and shows expected hit rate + estimated cost impact.

li: Simulate feature seems huge — show estimated fallback volume and incremental cost, flag customer-visible behaviors (latency, model change). Default simulation sample uses last 5m of traffic aggregated at route-level.

alex: Implementation note: simulation can reuse the existing trace-replay endpoint but must run at low priority. Add a rate cap in console to prevent abuse.

rachel: Small UX nit: default labels should avoid jargon. Use "Monitor-only", "Soft fallback (route to cheaper model)", "Hard fallback (block / simplified response)". Hover tooltips for reason codes.

deploy-bot: Experiment created: rollout/fallback-ui-sim-v1 by @maya — variant A shows "simulate" inline, variant B opens a modal. Experiment id: exp-20240502-42.

maya: Ok next steps: rachel will wire the compact policy JSON -> form mapping, alex will add hysteresis and billing flag hooks, sam will spec the audit retention + "capture now" flow, li will draft copy for the three main modes and the simulate results. I'll assemble a short mock for design review by EOD. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: one last ask — can we log the policy_id in the per-request trace so replay tools can filter by policy? saves a lot of triangulation later.

alex: yes, will add policy_id to trace header `X-RW-Policy` and include it in fallback events.

maya: perfect — closing this thread, will post the mock in #product after review.
